slides.text:
A loop runs the same block again and again. Rust has `loop`, which repeats until you stop it, and `while`, which repeats as long as a condition is true.

You will stop loops with `break`, skip a round with `continue`, and see that a `loop` can hand back a value.
Pseudo code, not Rust. Both loops are a block that repeats, and the difference is who decides when to stop.

`loop` has no condition: its block runs again as soon as it ends. Only `break` leaves it, so a `loop` without one never stops.

Pseudo code, not Rust.
`continue` ends the current round and jumps to the start of the next one. And `break` can carry a value, because a `loop` is an expression: that value is what the whole loop evaluates to.

exercises.guide: Repeat a block with `loop` and leave it with `break`.

The block repeats. Each round adds one and prints it, and the `if` ends the loop on the third.

notes.text: Repeats its block until a break.

exercises.title: Where does it stop?
exercises.guide: Follow the loop, then pick what is printed.
exercises.explanation: The check comes before the doubling. At 16 it is not above 20 yet, so n becomes 32, and only then does the `if` break.

exercises.title: A loop that returns a value
exercises.guide: Give `break` a value, and the loop evaluates to it.

chunks.guide: A counter for the attempts.
The loop is the value of `first_big`. When the condition holds, `break` hands out `tries`.

notes.text: The loop is an expression, so it can be assigned.
Stops the loop and returns tries.

chunks.guide: Print what the loop returned.

exercises.title: Return from a loop
exercises.guide: Name the variable that receives the loop, and hand back the first multiple of 5 that `n` reaches. The program prints it.

exercises.title: Skip a round
exercises.guide: Use `continue` to jump to the next round.

chunks.guide: A counter.
When n is 2, `continue` skips the print and starts the next round. The loop ends at 4.

notes.text: Skips the rest of this round.

chunks.guide: Runs after the loop.

slides.text:
`while` checks its condition before every round. If it is false at the start, the block never runs. The condition must be a `bool`, and the loop only ends when something in the block changes what it checks.

Pseudo code, not Rust.
A `while` loop that never changes what it checks never stops. When you use `continue`, make sure that change happens before it.

exercises.title: Count down
exercises.guide: Repeat a block while a condition is true.

chunks.guide: Where the countdown starts.
Each round prints the number and lowers it. The loop ends when it reaches 0.

notes.text: Checked before each round. False ends the loop.

chunks.guide: Runs when the loop is over.

exercises.title: Drain the battery
exercises.guide: Print the battery level and lower it every round. The output must be 10 and then 7, and nothing else.

exercises.title: Two conditions
exercises.guide: Combine conditions with `&&` so the loop stops on either limit.

chunks.guide: A running total and a round counter.
chunks.text:
let mut total = 0;
    let mut count = 0;

chunks.guide: The loop runs only while both checks hold. Whichever fails first ends it.

notes.text: True only when both sides are true.

chunks.guide: Print both values.

exercises.title: Overshooting the limit
exercises.guide: Follow the loop, then pick what is printed.
exercises.explanation: At 9 the condition is still true, so the block runs once more and n becomes 12. The check happens only at the start of a round.

exercises.title: Walk an array
exercises.guide: Use a counter as an index to visit every item.

chunks.guide: An array of scores.
An index and a sum, both starting at zero.
chunks.text:
let mut i = 0;
    let mut sum = 0;

chunks.guide: Add the item at `i`, then move to the next index. Stop when the index passes the last item.

notes.text: The number of items in the array.
The item at the current index.

chunks.guide: Print the sum.

exercises.title: Skip the refunds
exercises.guide: Update the index before `continue`, or the loop never ends.

chunks.guide: Order amounts, where a negative one is a refund, plus an index and a total.
The index grows first, so `continue` cannot skip it. Refunds jump to the next round without being added.

notes.text: True when the order is a refund.

chunks.guide: Print the total of the orders.

slides.text: Use `while` when the condition says it all, and `loop` when the end comes from the middle of the block or the loop must return a value.

exercises.title: Count the steps
exercises.guide: Count how many rounds a `while` needs to reach a goal.

chunks.guide: A starting number and a step counter.
chunks.text:
let mut n = 6;
    let mut steps = 0;

chunks.guide: Halve even numbers, and turn odd ones into 3n + 1. Count each round until n reaches 1.

notes.text: The loop runs until n becomes 1.

chunks.guide: Print how many steps it took.

exercises.title: Break in a nested loop
exercises.guide: Follow both loops, then pick what is printed.
exercises.explanation: The `break` leaves only the inner loop. The `while` goes on, and every round starts with a fresh inner.

chunks.guide: Four prices, a budget, what is spent and how many items fit.
Walk the prices. Break when the next one would go over the budget, otherwise buy it.

notes.text: What the total would be after buying this item.

chunks.guide: Print the count and the total.

exercises.title: What is it for?
exercises.guide: Pick what the loop is used for.
options: Counts the days a stock of 100 lasts at 15 a day
Finds how much is left after one day
Checks whether 100 is a multiple of 15
exercises.explanation: Each round uses up 15 and counts a day, until nothing is left. The counter ends as the number of days.

exercises.title: Only multiples of 3
exercises.guide: The program must print 3, 6 and 9 and nothing else. Every other number must cut its round short before the print, and the loop must still end.
